input.description: Show git-auth source and list files
Find callers of gitAuthArgs and remoteUrl usage
Show worktree, routes, api, config sources
Check package manifest and route wiring

input.reason: I checked the finding against the code, and it holds. In src/git-auth.ts:8, gitAuthArgs checks the host with `remoteUrl.includes("github.com")`. That is a substring test on the whole URL, not a check of the parsed hostname. So `https://github.com.evil.example/x.git` passes, and line 9 returns `http.extraHeader=Authorization: Bearer ${token}`. The only caller is cloneRepo (src/worktree.ts:15), which passes SERVICE_TOKEN (src/config.ts:4, from HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN) and runs `git -c http.extraHeader=... clone <remoteUrl>`, so git sends the header to whatever host the URL names. cloneRepo is called from registerRepo (src/routes.ts:18-22) with the user's `remoteUrl` straight from req.body. The only validation there is `if (!id || !remoteUrl) return { status: 400 }`. I found no host allowlist, URL parsing, tests or other guard anywhere in the repository that would block this.
input.summary: Substring host check sends the GitHub service token to lookalike remote hosts

findings.text: The host check is a substring match, so a remote URL such as `https://github.com.evil.example/x.git` passes and receives the service token in an `Authorization` header. Any user who can register a repository can collect the token.
findings.reason: Claim 1, the host check is a substring match: src/git-auth.ts:8 uses `remoteUrl.includes("github.com")` and never parses the hostname. Claim 2, `https://github.com.evil.example/x.git` passes and gets the service token in an Authorization header: that URL contains "github.com", so line 9 returns `["-c", `http.extraHeader=Authorization: Bearer ${token}`]`. src/worktree.ts:15 puts these args in front of `git clone repo.remoteUrl` with SERVICE_TOKEN from src/config.ts:4, so git sends the header to the attacker's host. Claim 3, any user who can register a repository can collect the token: registerRepo in src/routes.ts:18-22 reads remoteUrl from req.body, checks only that it is present, and passes it to cloneRepo. Nothing restricts the host.

evidence.code: await cloneRepo({ id, remoteUrl, owner: req.user.oid });

input.severity_reason: This is an exploitable security flaw that is easy to trigger. Any user who can register a repository can submit a URL that contains "github.com" but points to a host they control. The service's GitHub token (HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN) is then sent to that host in a Bearer header, which gives the attacker the service's GitHub credentials.
